AccessStatus.description:
Whether a source's full text could legitimately be retrieved.

The retrieval layer (E04) classifies every fetch into exactly one of these. There is no
"partially readable" state: a metered or truncated page is `PAYWALLED`, never `ACCESSIBLE`,
and nothing in the platform attempts to work around an access control.
AccessStatus.title: AccessStatus

Citation.description:
The cite for one card, with per-field provenance.

`authors` is a single field holding the ordered author list rather than one field per author,
because a page's byline is harvested (and verified) as a unit.

Resolution — harvesting these values from a snapshot's HTML and from Crossref — is the
citation service's job (E06); this model only records the outcome and its provenance.

author_credentials.description: Author qualification as stated on the source or in Crossref/ORCID; never inferred.

published_at_precision.description: How much of `published_at` its source states (`v1-e06-t13`). `year` and `month` mean the date is the first instant of that year or month and no day is known; `day`, the default, is what every cite stored before this field held, and is left out of the stored record.

accessed_at.description: When the platform retrieved the source.

authors_are_organizations.description: True when `authors` names the issuing organizations rather than people: the source named no person, and a typed source named the organization.
authors_are_organizations.title: Authors Are Organizations

cleared_by_student.description: Cite fields a student's last cite edit left empty, in cite order. Re-resolving the cite keeps each as the student left it; the edit policy rewrites the list on every cite edit.
cleared_by_student.title: Cleared By Student

CitationFieldSource.description:
Where one citation field's value was harvested from.

Recorded per field so an export can mark exactly which parts of a cite are unverified. A model
is never a source: authors, credentials, publications and dates are harvested deterministically
or left missing (architecture proposal §8).
CitationFieldSource.title: CitationFieldSource

DatePrecision.description:
How much of a publication date is known (v1-e07-t03; on an Article and a cite, v1-e06-t13).

Crossref deposits dates as `[year]`, `[year, month]` or `[year, month, day]`, and a user may state
a year or a month alone. A date known only to its year or month is stored at the first instant of
that period, and its precision says so, so nothing downstream reads an invented day. A precision is
never raised: a year stays a year.
DatePrecision.title: DatePrecision

ProvenanceMode.description:
Where a snapshot's or card's text came from.

This travels from the snapshot onto every card cut from it, so a reader can always tell
publisher-retrieved evidence from text a person supplied.
ProvenanceMode.title: ProvenanceMode

description:
An immutable record of one retrieval of one source.

A snapshot is the anchor of evidence integrity. It records the SHA-256 of the exact bytes that
came back, the SHA-256 of the deterministically normalized text derived from them, and the
versions of the code that produced each, so a card's evidence can be reconstructed and
re-checked later (architecture proposal §8, steps 1-2 and 5).

Blob keys are storage-neutral strings resolved by the `SnapshotStore` port, not S3 keys: V1
stores blobs on the local filesystem and V2 stores them in S3 without the entity changing.

Snapshots are never rewritten. `revision` therefore stays at 1; re-retrieving a source produces
a new snapshot rather than mutating this one.
